question: In an intrinsic semiconductor, the intrinsic carrier concentration is $2.0 \times 10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}$. Calculate the number density of electrons and holes. Also explain why both types of carriers are present.

options.A: For an intrinsic semiconductor, $n_e=n_h=n_i$. Hence $n_e=2.0\times10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}$ and $n_h=2.0\times10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}$. Thermal breaking of one covalent bond creates one free electron and one hole simultaneously, so both carriers are present in equal numbers.
options.B: $n_e=2.0\times10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}$ and $n_h=0$, because intrinsic semiconductor contains only electrons.
options.C: $n_e=4.0\times10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}$ and $n_h=1.0\times10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}$, because holes are formed separately from electrons.
options.D: $n_e=0$ and $n_h=2.0\times10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}$, because all thermal energy creates holes only.
